title: Felix and the Will
premise: Xanthe Oyelaran, a night dispatcher who treats every fare as a case to be closed, receives two letters in the same week: one confessing to a hit-and-run that killed a courier named Ada Voss, and one promising 'more, if you keep listening.' The letters lead Xanthe into the city's taxi ledgers — where fares, routes, and tips encode a hidden record of who paid for Ada's death and why. As the trial of the confessed driver approaches, Xanthe realizes the confession is a purchased shield for someone higher up, and that decoding the ledger will cost them the anonymity their survival has always depended on. In the end, Xanthe chooses justice outside the law: they hand the decoded ledger not to the police but to Ada's estranged sister, letting the truth detonate publicly on the trial's final day.
about_author: Orsen Halloran spent eleven years driving night shifts in a mid-sized city before turning to fiction, and his mysteries are known for their insider texture of radio static, dead runs, and drivers who see everything. He writes under a pen name because, as he puts it, 'a dispatcher's best tool is being nobody.'

chapters.title: The Two Letters
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. During a slow Tuesday shift, two letters arrive at the dispatch office: a full confession to killing courier Ada Voss, signed by driver Marcus Teale, and an unsigned note reading 'More if you keep listening.' Xanthe, who can't resist an unsolved case, pockets both. Beat: curiosity curdling into unease.

chapters.title: Dead Run
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Xanthe pulls the dispatch logs from the night Ada died and finds Marcus's cab logged three miles from where her body was found — a route no dispatcher would assign. The first letter's details don't match the log. Someone wrote a false confession. Beat: the thrill of the hunt.

chapters.title: The Ledger in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Reviewing the company's old paper ledgers, Xanthe notices recurring anomalous entries: identical fares, impossible tips, routes that loop past Ada's old workplace. They begin copying pages, sensing a pattern but unable to read it. Beat: obsession taking root.

chapters.title: Marcus at the Wheel
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Awaiting trial, Marcus insists he never hit anyone but admits he took money to say he did. He remembers only a voice on the phone giving him a pickup address. His fear isn't prison — it's whoever paid him finding out he talked. Beat: dread beneath bravado.

chapters.title: Keep Listening
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. A second unsigned letter arrives with a single ledger page number circled. Cross-referencing it, Xanthe finds every flagged entry was dispatched by the same supervisor ID — one belonging to a man who retired rich two years ago, Denny Kroll. Beat: first real thread.

chapters.title: Ada's Sister
chapters.summary: Nadia Voss's POV. Nadia, a paralegal preparing for the trial she believes will finally close her sister's case, is contacted by an anonymous tipster — Xanthe, guarded, offering fragments. She doesn't trust them but can't look away. Beat: grief weaponized into hope.

chapters.title: Radio Silence
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Xanthe's supervisor warns them off 'old paper' after someone requests the archived ledgers by name. That night a cab tails Xanthe home. The hunter realizes they've become the quarry. Beat: fear sharpening focus.

chapters.title: What the Tips Meant
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Decoding breakthrough: the inflated tips aren't payment — they're timestamps. Each flagged entry marks a night a specific vehicle was 'cleaned' — evidence destroyed or witnesses paid. Ada's death was one entry among dozens. Beat: horror at the scale.

chapters.title: The Voice on the Phone
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Marcus's lawyer pushes him to plead guilty for a lighter sentence. Alone, Marcus replays the phone call that recruited him and recognizes a verbal tic — the same phrasing Xanthe uses on dispatch radio. He starts to wonder who else was listening that night. Beat: paranoia.

chapters.title: Kroll's Quiet Life
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Xanthe surveils Denny Kroll, now a respected charity board member, and watches him meet a current company executive — meaning the ledger's author may still be active inside the firm. Beat: the conspiracy has a present tense.

chapters.title: A Fare Named Witness
chapters.summary: Nadia's POV. Nadia tracks down a former driver mentioned in the ledger who fled the city years ago. He tells her about 'the cleaner's rate' — double fare, no questions — and warns her to stop before the trial. That night her apartment is searched. Beat: the cost of asking.

chapters.title: Burn the Books
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The archive room catches fire — ruled electrical. Xanthe, having anticipated it, already photographed everything but loses the physical originals that could authenticate them in court. Beat: setback; the law's doors closing.

chapters.title: Confession, Revised
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Marcus recants on the stand's eve, telling his lawyer about the phone call and the money. Within hours his protective custody is revoked on a clerical error. Beat: the machinery protecting itself.

chapters.title: The Dispatcher's Code
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Xanthe cracks the ledger's final layer: the entries were written by two hands over years — Kroll recording, and someone above him authorizing. The authorization initials match the company's founder-adjacent figure, Emeric Saul. Beat: vertigo at the top of the chain.

chapters.title: Keep Listening, Part Two
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. A third letter arrives, handwritten this time, revealing the correspondent is inside the company and terrified — likely the second hand in the ledger. It names a meeting place: the depot, 3 a.m., between fares. Beat: hope laced with trap-sense.

chapters.title: Three A.M. at the Depot
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The informant is a retired dispatcher who kept carbon copies of everything Kroll filed. Mid-handoff, a car sweeps the lot; the informant flees, shoving a satchel into Xanthe's cab. Xanthe drives away with the whole archive on the passenger seat. Beat: point of no return.

chapters.title: What Survival Costs
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV, reflective. Hiding in a motel, Xanthe confronts their own history: years ago they stayed silent about a fleet owner's crimes to keep their job — the silence that let the ledger system grow. Their pride in 'closing cases' was penance. Beat: reckoning with complicity.

chapters.title: Nadia's Decision
chapters.summary: Nadia's POV. Nadia receives copies of everything and faces a choice: give it to prosecutors, who've already shown they can be leaned on, or release it herself. She chooses the courtroom — but on her terms, as an intervention, not evidence. Beat: agency reclaimed.

chapters.title: The Trial's Last Day
chapters.summary: Alternating Xanthe/Nadia POV. As the verdict nears on Marcus, Nadia stands during proceedings and reads the ledger's decoded entries aloud, naming Kroll and Saul while Xanthe simultaneously sends the full archive to every news desk in the city. Beat: controlled detonation.

chapters.title: Aftermath in Static
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Kroll is arrested trying to flee; Saul's lawyers circle but the company collapses under scrutiny. Marcus walks free but broken, exonerated and unemployable. The informant resurfaces alive. Xanthe keeps dispatching nights, waiting for consequences. Beat: exhausted clarity.

chapters.title: One More Letter
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. A final envelope arrives: empty except for a single taxi receipt dated the night Ada died — from a car the ledger never listed. Someone out there remains unclosed. Xanthe pins it above the radio. Beat: vigilance as identity.

chapters.title: Felix and the Will
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The title's meaning lands: Felix, the depot's ancient three-legged cat everyone feeds, outlasted every owner of the company — and so does the will to know. Xanthe takes a new fare, closes the case file on Ada Voss, and answers the next call. Beat: quiet, earned resolve.
